lines.text: Eight days. Anaya went to the shop at the end of the lane.
She had walked past it a hundred times without going in.
There it was. The big box. The one that goes up like a tree.
Forty rupees, she said. I have forty-two.
She put every coin on the counter.
It's the festival, the shopkeeper said. The price went up.
She counted her coins one more time, as if they might have grown.
She picked them up, and she walked home.
There's one box left at the old price.
But it's promised to somebody else.
